summary: Reishis hageiz, the first wool sheared from sheep, is given to the Kohen. It applies everywhere and always, but not to korbanos. The foreleg, cheeks and stomach apply to more animals than reishis hageiz.

chunks.he: רֵאשִׁית הַגֵּז נוֹהֵג בָּאָרֶץ וּבְחוּצָה לָאָרֶץ,
chunks.en: Reishis hageiz applies in Eretz Yisrael and outside Eretz Yisrael,
chunks.explain: The first wool sheared from the sheep, given to the Kohen.
chunks.st: The mitzva of the first sheared wool that every Jew must give to the priest, as stated in the verse: “And the first sheared wool of your flock [tzonekha] shall you give him” (Deuteronomy 18:4), applies both in Eretz Yisrael and outside of Eretz Yisrael,

chunks.en: when the Beis HaMikdash stands and when it does not,
chunks.st: in the presence of the Temple and not in the presence of the Temple, and

chunks.en: with plain animals but not with korbanos.
chunks.st: with regard to non-sacred animals. But it does not apply to sacrificial animals.

chunks.he: חֹמֶר בַּזְּרוֹעַ וּבַלְּחָיַיִם וּבַקֵּבָה מֵרֵאשִׁית הַגֵּז,
chunks.en: The foreleg, cheeks, and stomach are stricter than reishis hageiz,
chunks.st: There are more stringent elements in the mitzva of the foreleg, the jaw, and the maw (see 130a) than in the halakha of the first sheared wool

chunks.he: שֶׁהַזְּרוֹעַ וְהַלְּחָיַיִם וְהַקֵּבָה נוֹהֲגִים בְּבָקָר וּבְצֹאן,
chunks.en: because the foreleg, cheeks, and stomach apply to cattle and to sheep,
chunks.st: in that the mitzva of the foreleg, the jaw, and the maw applies to cattle and to sheep,
chunks.stMore: as it is written: “Whether it be ox or sheep, that he shall give unto the priest the foreleg, and the jaw, and the maw” (Deuteronomy 18:3);

chunks.en: to many animals and to few.
chunks.st: and it applies to numerous animals and to few animals.

chunks.he: וְרֵאשִׁית הַגֵּז אֵינוֹ נוֹהֵג אֶלָּא בִרְחֵלוֹת,
chunks.en: But reishis hageiz applies only to sheep,
chunks.st: But by contrast, the mitzva of the first sheared wool applies only to sheep and not to goats and cattle,

chunks.en: and applies only when there are many.
chunks.st: and applies only to numerous animals.

summary: Beis Shammai and Beis Hillel argue how many sheep make "many" for reishis hageiz. The mishnah also says how much wool to give the Kohen, and who gives it when wool is sold.

chunks.en: And how many is "many"?
chunks.st: And how many are numerous?

chunks.en: Beis Shammai say:
chunks.st: Beit Shammai say:

chunks.en: Two sheep,
chunks.st: It is at least two sheep,

chunks.en: as it says (Yeshayahu 7):
chunks.st: as it is stated: “

chunks.he: יְחַיֶּה אִישׁ עֶגְלַת בָּקָר וּשְׁתֵּי צֹאן.
chunks.en: "A man will raise a young cow and two sheep."
chunks.st: That a man shall rear a young cow, and two sheep [tzon]” (Isaiah 7:21),
chunks.stMore: indicating that two sheep are characterized as tzon; and the mitzva of the first sheared wool is written using the term “your flock [tzonekha].”

chunks.en: And Beis Hillel say:
chunks.st: And Beit Hillel say:

chunks.en: Five, as it says (Shmuel I 25):
chunks.st: It is at least five sheep, as it is stated: “

chunks.en: "Five sheep, made ready."
chunks.st: And five sheep [tzon] made” (I Samuel 25:18).

chunks.en: Rabbi Dosa ben Harkinas says:
chunks.st: Rabbi Dosa ben Harkinas says:

chunks.he: חָמֵשׁ רְחֵלוֹת גּוֹזְזוֹת מָנֶה מָנֶה וּפְרָס,
chunks.en: Five sheep that each give a maneh and a half of wool
chunks.explain: A maneh is a weight of one hundred dinars.
chunks.st: When shearing five sheep, the sheared wool of each sheep weighing one hundred dinars each and half [peras] of one hundred dinars each, i.e., one hundred and fifty dinars each,

chunks.en: must give reishis hageiz.
chunks.st: are subject to the obligation of the first sheared wool,
chunks.stMore: i.e., they render the owner obligated to give the first sheared wool to the priests.

chunks.en: And the Sages say:
chunks.st: And the Rabbis say:

chunks.en: Five sheep that give any amount of wool.
chunks.st: Any five sheep, each of whose sheared wool weighs any amount, render the owner obligated in the mitzva.

chunks.en: And how much do we give him?
chunks.st: And how much of the sheared wool does one give to the priest?

chunks.en: The weight of five sela'im in Yehudah,
chunks.explain: A sela is a coin, used here as a weight.
chunks.st: One gives him sheared wool of the weight of five sela in Judea,

chunks.en: which are ten sela'im in the Galil,
chunks.st: which are the equivalent of ten sela in the Galilee,
chunks.stMore: as the weight of the Galilean sela is half that of the Judean sela.

chunks.en: washed and not dirty,
chunks.st: Furthermore, although one may give the wool to the priest without laundering it, this must be the weight of the wool once laundered and not when sullied,
chunks.stMore: as is characteristic of wool when sheared.

chunks.en: enough to make a small garment from it,
chunks.st: The measure that must be given to the priest is enough to fashion a small garment from it,

chunks.en: as it says (Devarim 18):
chunks.st: as it is stated: “

chunks.en: "You shall give him,"
chunks.st: Shall you give him” (Deuteronomy 18:4),

chunks.en: so that it is enough to be a gift.
chunks.st: indicating that the sheared wool must contain enough for a proper gift.

chunks.he: לֹא הִסְפִּיק לִתְּנוֹ לוֹ עַד שֶׁצְּבָעוֹ,
chunks.en: If he did not get to give it to him before he dyed it,
chunks.st: If the owner of the shearing did not manage to give it to the priest until he dyed it, the owner is

chunks.en: he is free. If he washed it but did not dye it,
chunks.st: exempt from the mitzva of the first sheared wool, as this constitutes a change in the wool by which means he acquires ownership of it. If he laundered it but did not dye it, he is

chunks.he: חַיָּב. הַלּוֹקֵחַ גֵּז צֹאנוֹ שֶׁל נָכְרִי,
chunks.en: he must give. Someone who buys the wool of a non-Jew's sheep
chunks.st: obligated to give the first sheared wool, as laundering does not constitute a change in the wool. One who purchases the fleece of the sheep of a gentile

chunks.en: is free from reishis hageiz.
chunks.st: is exempt from the obligation of giving the first sheared wool to the priest.

chunks.en: Someone who buys the wool of his friend's sheep:
chunks.st: With regard to one who purchases the fleece of the sheep of another Jew,

chunks.en: if the seller kept some,
chunks.st: if the seller kept some of the wool, then

chunks.en: the seller must give.
chunks.st: the seller is obligated to give the first sheared wool to the priest. If the seller

chunks.en: If he did not keep any,
chunks.st: did not keep any of the wool,

chunks.en: the buyer must give.
chunks.st: the buyer is obligated to give it. If the seller

chunks.en: If he had two kinds,
chunks.st: had two types of sheep,

chunks.en: gray ones and white ones,
chunks.st: gray and white,

chunks.he: מָכַר לוֹ שְׁחוּפוֹת אֲבָל לֹא לְבָנוֹת,
chunks.en: and he sold him the gray but not the white,
chunks.st: and he sold the buyer the gray fleece but not the white fleece,

chunks.en: or the males but not the females:
chunks.st: or if he sold the fleece of the male sheep but not of the female sheep, then

chunks.he: זֶה נוֹתֵן לְעַצְמוֹ וְזֶה נוֹתֵן לְעַצְמוֹ:
chunks.en: this one gives for himself, and that one gives for himself.
chunks.st: this one, the seller, gives the first sheared wool for himself to the priest from the wool that he kept, and that one, the buyer, gives the first sheared wool for himself to the priest from the wool that he bought.
